articleTitle: DSSS system employing a class of modulatable complex spreading sequences
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of a Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) system employing a class of modulatable complex spreading sequences is presented. Several digital signal processing design problems are highlighted, and a novel constant-amplitude filtering procedure for a class of complex chirp-like spreading sequences is proposed. A proposed receiver block diagram is given, and some simulation results are shown to verify correct system operation in both single and multi-user environments.

articleTitle: Practical performance specification for a class of saturating systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A method of closed loop performance specification for linear time invariant, stable, minimum-phase systems with multiple saturating elements is developed. Necessary constraints on the closed loop transfer function are determined which ensure that no saturation occurs in the actuator signal and derivatives of the output. Examples demonstrating the technique are presented.

articleTitle: The formal descriptive technique sdl in software engineering
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Formal descriptive techniques provide a means to describe and manage the behaviour and structure of complex systems. In the last few years powerful commercial tool support for the formal descriptive technique SDL (Specification and Description Language) became available. This allows for the practical application of SDL in the software engineering process. A brief overview of the SDL language is given. The basic SDL concepts available to describe the structure and behaviour of systems are also explained. The typical capabilities of tools are listed and industrial experience with SDL is described. A comprehensive list of references identifies the available information on SDL.

articleTitle: Object based software development: Practice and pitfalls
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Experience points to substantial benefits in using object technology (OT) based approaches to software construction for large, heterogeneous distributed systems. The ability to reuse existing design knowledge that is captured within properties of software artifacts is one of the major benefits. This knowledge is embodied within frameworks that are supported by design patterns. Notwithstanding the alluring nature of OT, its undisciplined use may lead to pitfalls, manifested as increased software complexity. These pitfalls may be addressed by architecting the software artifacts and by ensuring that developers are suitably trained.

articleTitle: Evaluation of low frequency magnetic fields in low cost dwellings
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents the results of a survey which investigated the level of magnetic fields in informal housing in South Africa. The construction and wiring of a typical informal dwelling was established and a test dwelling was built. The magnetic field in the dwelling was measured at twelve locations under different conditions. The effect of the construction materials, wiring practice and appliance choice is noted. A further survey of the levels of magnetic fields in twenty residences in an informal settlement in Ivory Park is described. The results of the survey are compared to those of previous South African and Australian studies which were performed exclusively on formal dwellings. The paper shows that both previous and future international and South African research can be applied to the informal settlement case as there is no significant difference between the informal and formal dwelling results.

articleTitle: 1985–1995: Ten years of transactions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: More than ten years ago the SAIEE launched a project to adapt its publications to the requirements of its membership. This resulted in the previous Transactions (prior to 1986) being split into two publications, i.e. “Elektron” and the Transactions of the SAIEE. In keeping with current international tendencies, the “Transactions” was then planned as publishing current research and development activities, subject to international peer review. An international editorial panel of associate editors was set up, and in January 1985 the first issue of this new style publication of the SAIEE saw the light (vol. 76, No. 1).

articleTitle: A discipline of software architecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Neither software engineering nor software design qualifies as a discipline, but software architecture might. Action-centered design is proposed as the means to build software architecture by joining the two.

articleTitle: Reuse of legacy software in object-oriented re-engineering: A case study
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: There appear to be formidable obstacles to reuse when using the object-oriented paradigm to re-engineer legacy software developed using the structured paradigm. These obstacles are a consequence of the fundamental differences between the structured paradigm and the object-oriented paradigm. Nevertheless, as demonstrated by the case study presented here, it is possible to achieve reuse of specifications, design, code, and test cases. A high proportion of code reuse was achieved because the legacy software was written in C and the re-engineered software in C++, a syntactic superset of C. At the module level, reuse of 100% was obtained. Worldwide, there is more legacy software written in COBOL than in any other language. The results of this paper may have implications for the re-engineering of COBOL legacy software in OO-COBOL, the syntactic superset of COBOL to be standardized in 1997.

articleTitle: DPSK performance of a Nakagami faded DS/SSMA system with diversity
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This work considers the performance of Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum Multiple Access (DS/SSMA) transmission with space- and time diversity for the uplink of a cellular Indoor Wireless Communication (IWC) channel. Due to fading associated with the IWC channel and the asynchronous arrival of the received signals a coherent reference is difficult to obtain and hence Differential Phase Shift Keying(DPSK) is assumed as modulation scheme. The indoor communication channel, which is multipath faded, is modeled by a discrete set of Nakagami faded paths which has been shown to fit empirical data of the IWC channel better than other distributions [1]. Instead of using the commonly assumed Gaussian Assumption to describe the Inter User Interference (IUI), the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) method [2] is used to infer the IUI distribution accurately [3]. The average error rate and capacity of a DS/SSMA system under typical IWC channel conditions is therefore accurately calculated using the IUI distribution obtained by the MaxEnt method. Numerical results reveal that for non-diversity receivers, Nakagami fading is very hostile to the SSMA signal. However, using space diversity with Maximum Ratio Combining (MRC) and time diversity (in the form of convolutional coding) at the base station, the average error rate can be reduced dramatically, allowing for reliable communication.

articleTitle: Embedded fuzzy controller for a DC locomotive
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Embedded fuzzy controllers enhance and complement existing conventional controllers with intelligent functions derived from human control operator experience. Whenever the system to be controlled is highly nonlinear, parameters time-variant with, and certain features are too difficult or cumbersome to model, fuzzy controllers circumvent the difficulties associated with conventional mathematical modelling. This paper discusses the recently developed embedded fuzzy controller of Spoomet's Class 6E/6E1 3kV DC locomotive, which was developed to prevent the damage during starting as a result of uncontrolled wheel slip and incorrect taking up of slack. The results presented herein were achieved by using locomotive and load models and verified by both simulation and exhaustive in-service testing on a real locomotive.

articleTitle: Development of a rogowski coil to measure lightning current impulses
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper aims to present the basic theory of a Rogowski coil used to measure lightning current impulses. A model of the Rogowski coil and the associated passive integrator circuit is presented and a technique for designing a Rogowski coil for a given application is described. The design technique requires the designer to specify the required gain, winding former dimensions and permissible measurement error for a given current waveform. These are used to obtain the number of turns on the coil and the values of the passive integrator resistor and capacitor required. The implications of these specifications on the voltage stress applied to the coil is also discussed. The procedure is used to design a Rogowski coil which can be used to measure three different standard current impulses.

articleTitle: Present and future trends in power electronic converter development
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The development of various aspects of the technology of electronic power conversion is examined. The present state of the art is reviewed, giving attention to generic issues rather than to detail. This evaluation reviews power electronic devices, components, packaging and cooling, as well as present power electronic converter technology, including snubbers, resonant converters, resonant transition converters, current fed, voltage fed, direct and minimum converters. The present trends are identified and particularly related to packaging and cooling technology, manufacturing technology, environmental impact technology and converter electromagnetics. The future possibilities of electronic power converter technology is discussed in relation to packaging and cooling, environmental impact - including materials and EMI/EMC - manufacturing technology and converter electromagnetics.

Author Keywords: review of state of the art power electronics

articleTitle: Explicit and implicit inter-object communication
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Serious use of object technology involves a software development process based upon one of the various methods advocated in the literature and frequently supported by a CASE tool. The methods and associated tools rely on the use of particular notations during analysis and design phases: usually some form of relationship diagram to express a so-called static object model of the envisaged system; and state charts to depict a dynamic model. The dynamic model is meant to express object behaviour that results from inter-object communication (IOC). The intention is that these models should seamlessly carry over to inform and guide the implementation phase. In general, commonly-used notations for the static object model seem to serve their purpose well. However, there is some doubt about the efficacy of dynamic model notations, particularly the state chart variety used in OMT. The problem is intimately associated with IOC in which so-called inter-object conditions play a part. State-of-the-art mechanisms to handle such inter-object conditions at an implementation level appear to be inadequate. Several alternative solutions to the problem are proposed and evaluated.

articleTitle: The application of the Monte Carlo method to semiconductor simulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A short tutorial on the application of the Monte Carlo method to semiconductor material and device simulations is presented. Its relevance and importance as a tool for microwave device analyses are discussed. A device simulation program based on this method has been developed. The results of both a GaAs bulk material analysis and a GaAs-diode device simulation are presented.

articleTitle: A visual method for real-time software engineering
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The Engineering of Real-Time Systems requires specification, design, implementation of software components, within a project development framework for optimal development effort, re-use and maintainability. This multitude of requirements lead to a suite of languages which addresses the engineering aspects of real-time systems. The data flow architecture was chosen as a generic architecture based on the investigations into system architectures. The work is important as it provides a suite of languages which can support the real-time engineering process from specification to implementation and at the same time an unambiguous description of each software component at each development level. The paper examines the multiple dimensions required to describe a software component, proposes languages for the purpose, looks at the inter-relationship between the languages and closes with an example application.

articleTitle: An adaptive fuzzy logic speed control of high performance motor drives suitable for low-cost microprocessor based implementations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper presents a fuzzy logic (FL) based adaptive control technique for variable speed drives using a recursive-least-square identification algorithm and an original tuning method of the FL speed controller. The input and output gains of the FL speed controller are adjusted on-line according to changes in system parameters, whereas the control rule base and the membership functions of fuzzy sets are kept unchanged. The equations which give the dependence of FL controller gains on system parameters are founded on a parallel study of FL and PI controllers, being used in the tuning process of the FL speed controller. The performance of the proposed adaptive FL control system was tested by simulation studies and practical experiments. Implementation aspects of converter fed motor drive systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Guest editorial: Special issue on software engineering
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Despite the best efforts of the best minds we are still not able to write reliable, economical and efficient software systems with the same ease that engineers build bridges. This Special Issue of the Transactions on Software Engineering therefore offers no panacea either and merely highlights some of the problems and partial solutions.
